newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM backs Latvian efforts to join CEFTA.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM backs Latvian efforts to join CEFTA.

text.p: Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Thursday that the Czech Republic would support Latvia's attemps to join the Central European Freed Trade Agreement by next year.

"Premier Klaus... promised the support of the Czech Republic in the attempts of Latvia to enter (CEFTA), in which Latvia could become a member already next year," Klaus's office said a statement issued after a meeting with Latvian foreign minister Valdis Birkavs in Prague.

CEFTA -- formed after the fall of communism to faciliate free trade between the former communist contries of Central Europe -- currently includes Poland, Hungary, Slovakia, Slovenia, and the Czech Republic.
Several Baltic and Balkan countries have shown an interest in joining the group.
The statement said that Birkavs discussed the possibilities for Czech companies interested in Riga's privatisation of industrial firms and financing of a rail corridor.
